item.title: Oregon court now upholds $810,000 award over 2018 tree clearing beyond a neighbour's property line
item.description: In an Oregon land dispute, a property owner accused their neighbor of intentionally clearing land past established boundaries. A jury sided with the plaintiff, awarding them $810,000 in damages. The court upheld this decision, indicating that the defendants failed to provide valid evidence to counter their liability, while also noting that Bosma was aware of the boundary issues before the clearing took place.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Julia Child Home Sells: former Cambridge house fetches $6.525 million; kitchen lives on at Smithsonian
item.description: Julia Child’s iconic home in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has found a new owner for $6.525 million. This historic residence, adored for its connection to Child's culinary shows, has seen extensive renovations. The original kitchen, however, remains untouched and is now a cherished exhibit at the Smithsonian Museum. To honor her legacy, a commemorative plaque is set to be installed at the site, ensuring that Child's influence on cooking continues.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: US wildlife teams surveyed six offshore islands for invasive species, finding rats on five and iguanas on one; the results will guide future work to protect nesting seabirds
item.description: Recent surveys in the U.S. Virgin Islands have identified invasive species on several offshore cays. Black rats and green iguanas pose significant threats to local seabird populations, such as the red-billed tropicbird. Conservationists are now evaluating strategies to eradicate these non-native animals from the islands. Removal efforts could lead to improved nesting conditions for seabirds in the future. Successful initiatives may help restore these vital habitats for future generations.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Georgia court upholds waste facility permit as 97 planned townhomes still unbuilt at permit filing
item.description: A developer in Bartow County, Georgia challenged a permit for a nearby waste processing facility. The county approved the permit despite concerns that it violated zoning restrictions. The developer argued that their planned townhomes should receive protection under existing zoning laws. However, the court found that the definitions of residential dwellings applied only to already constructed buildings. Ultimately, the appeals court upheld the permit, allowing the waste facility to operate.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Luke Bryan's Farm Tour awards 97 college scholarships and helps provide 11 million meals since 2009
item.description: Since its inception in 2009, Luke Bryan's Farm Tour has championed educational opportunities by awarding 97 scholarships and supplying over 11 million meals for needy families. Partnering with Bayer’s #HerestotheFarmer campaign, the initiative bridges support between farming families and communities. Attendees also donated nearly 20,000 pounds of food to hunger-relief efforts, underscoring a commitment to enhancing education and food accessibility in agricultural areas nationwide.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: She runs a Caribbean takeaway in England and gives free meals to people who cannot afford them; 71-year-old Florence ‘Mama Flo’ Coke has become a local hero.
item.description: Florence Coke runs a Caribbean takeaway in Stockport, where she offers free meals for the needy. She has been inspired by her parents' tradition of helping the poor in Jamaica. During the COVID-19 crisis, she continued to feed struggling families with free meals and food parcels. Recently, she was recognized with a Local Hero award for her community service efforts.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Washington court upholds deal after couple split again, leaving wife without bank and stock assets
item.description: A couple from Washington navigated a messy divorce settlement only to remarry, before the cycle of separation began once more. The court upheld an arbitration ruling that favored William Gibbs, denying Joy the assets previously awarded. Although Joy retained some funds from her BNY Mellon 401(k), she forfeited half of the USAA accounts and restricted stock units.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas Farm Funds Scholarships: Donated land backs Gruver High students; many are first-generation grads
item.description: In Gruver, Texas, a remarkable farming initiative has turned inherited land into a thriving source of scholarship funds for local students. By pooling their resources, farmers and community members cultivate crops that have raised around $3 million for education since 2012, benefitting nearly 300 students, including first-generation college graduates like Sydney Ortiz and Rhett Sparks.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘I guess I’m dead’: Tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson's chilling post resurfaces
item.description: In a heartbreaking incident, tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson and his family lost their lives in a Florida plane crash on November 1, 2026. The tragedy claimed all nine individuals aboard the private jet. Robinson, known for his sarcastic social media presence, previously founded notable marketing technology companies. The National Transportation Safety Board has initiated an investigation into the cause of the fatal accident.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pennsylvania court upholds borough's duty to maintain steps after 130 years of public use
item.description: A couple from Jim Thorpe filed a lawsuit against their borough regarding the maintenance of public steps. They argued that the borough had historically maintained the steps, which had been used for over 130 years. The Commonwealth Court upheld the lower court's ruling that affirmed the borough's maintenance obligation. Evidence included historical records showing the borough's involvement in repairs and maintenance over the years.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A British family doctor was convicted of murdering 15 patients
item.description: Harold Shipman, a general practitioner in England, was infamously convicted for the murder of numerous patients. His reputation as a trusted doctor gave him unfettered access to the homes of vulnerable elderly individuals, leading to a devastating series of crimes. An extensive investigation later uncovered that Shipman was linked to the deaths of at least 215 people over many years.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California court allows grandfather five-minute monthly calls, rejects mother's $17,193 fee bid
item.description: Timothy S sought court-ordered visitation with his granddaughter after Sarah H regained custody of the children. He had raised the older child for nearly two years prior to this change in custody. The trial court allowed only a brief monthly telephone call while denying Sarah's request for legal fees tied to the case. California's Court of Appeal upheld this decision, affirming the lower court's interpretation of the law.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Jen Lilley revives Christmas Is Not Cancelled toy drive for kids
item.description: Jen Lilley, the acclaimed actress, has relaunched her Christmas Is Not Cancelled campaign to aid children in need, setting a goal of delivering 20,000 gifts to underprivileged youth this Christmas. By letting parents select the gifts, the initiative preserves their dignity. Furthermore, podcaster Shawn Ryan's generous $30,000 donation will provide bikes and scooters. The campaign is now a nonprofit, making financial contributions tax-deductible.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: NASA's Hubble studied dwarf galaxies and found they kept just 11% of the oxygen made by their stars
item.description: A recent investigation revealed that dwarf galaxies only retain an average of 11% of the oxygen generated by their stars. The remaining oxygen likely escapes into space during powerful supernova explosions. This finding indicates that smaller galaxies have greater difficulty retaining their materials than previously believed. Researchers plan to conduct further studies to examine where this missing oxygen ultimately ends up.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: ‘Expect new dynamics’: Ukraine hopes for more support after Democrats sweep midterms
item.description: Ukraine anticipates enhanced military and financial assistance from the United States after the midterm elections. Foreign minister Andrii Sybiha expressed hope for new dynamics and support from the incoming Democratic majority. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy acknowledged the Democrats' vocal backing of Ukraine since their election success. This shift in power could enable legislation favoring aid to Ukraine despite previous limitations.
